title: The wiring sets a phase-blind quantum memory's gap, the weight caps its coherence
authors: Ruini Qian, Zhaobin Lyu, Zelong Yin, Jingjing Hu, Dengfeng Li, Shuoming An
abstract: Engineered dissipation corrects errors, yet a memory's phase decays. What the memory's gap measures is not settled. Here we show that when each jump resets one basis state, the wiring can set the gap time while the phase keeps its rate. Under dephasing the gap time spans two orders across wirings; the phase does not. In this class, a contrast on two or more qubits fades faster than a bare qubit at any distance; no such pump power substitutes. The ceiling is two over the qubits the contrast spans. A two-branch pump can escape it at distance three; a two-clock test runs on published data.
summary: This work analyzes the decoherence mechanisms in a quantum memory stabilized by engineered dissipation. It demonstrates that the dissipation structure controls the population decay rate (the gap time) but leaves the phase coherence decay rate determined by the underlying bare noise. This reveals that the memory functions on two distinct, decoupled timescales.
main_problem: The paper investigates which physical parameter—the memory's gap time or the stored phase coherence—is determined by the engineered dissipation (the 'wiring') in a quantum memory.
main_result: The wiring sets the gap time ($	ext{T}_{	ext{gap}}$), while the phase coherence ($	ext{T}_{	ext{X}}$) retains its intrinsic decay rate, implying the memory operates on two independent timescales.
method: The analysis uses the Lindblad dissipator formalism to compare the decay rates of the code-space population versus the off-diagonal coherence elements.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum memory modeled on a plaquette structure using engineered dissipation (a 'pump') to stabilize a code space, analyzed via the Liouvillian superoperator.
key_observables: Gap Time ($	ext{T}_{	ext{gap}}$), Phase Coherence Lifetime ($	ext{T}_{	ext{X}}$), Logical Weight ($w$), and the coherence decay rate ($\eta$).
important_parameters: The ratio $\eta = 	ext{T}_{	ext{X}}/	ext{T}_1$, and the weight-dependent bound $\eta \le 2/w$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the pump jump resets one basis state, and it distinguishes between the population decay sector and the coherence decay sector.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase-contrast boundary ($\eta$ vs. $w$) showing the coherence bound, and show the decay of population ($\langle P_C angle$) remaining high while coherence ($\langle  ar{X} angle$) decays much faster.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by analyzing the Liouvillian dynamics, deriving bounds on coherence decay based on weight, and contrasting the resulting gap time (set by the pump) against the coherence lifetime (set by bare noise).
why_interesting: It provides a detailed theoretical understanding of how engineered dissipation can stabilize the population state (gap) independently of the phase coherence, a crucial distinction for building robust quantum memories.
